title: Pre-Market (early edition) — Tuesday, Nov 17, 2026
html:
Early edition, written about 12:40 AM ET; Europe hasn't opened and futures can change a lot before 9:30.

Futures are flat, Asia sold chips on a new US export rule, and none of it matters as much as what Nvidia says at about 4:20 PM. We go into it leaning short, with two act-now puts and one broken call to clean up.

The one thing

Nvidia reports at about 4:20 PM ET (call at 5:00), and its weekly options price a move of about $15 either way (about 9.7%, roughly $141 to $171 from Monday's $156.14 close). The Street expects about $109 billion in revenue and $2.47 a share, against the company's own guide of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%. With Colette Kress running her first report as interim CEO, the Q4 guide and the gross margin (she pointed to 71–72% in August) matter more than the beat.

My read: the stock is already priced for bad news. It is down 27% in a month and closed 81 cents above your 0.5 ($155.33). A merely clean report can squeeze the AI names higher tonight, and that is the main risk to our short-leaning book. It is not a reason to skip setups that are already confirmed; it is a reason to know which plays are exposed (below). What would change my mind: SPY reclaiming $745 during the day. Then I stop adding puts ahead of the print.

  • Nasdaq 100 futures (10:50 PM): +0.5%
  • Dow futures (10:37 PM): -0.3%

  • IWM overnight: $272.17 -0.3%
  • RSP equal-weight: $218.93 +0.0%
  • SMH chips overnight: $466.34 +1.0%

  • 2-yr yield (Mon close): 4.82% -3 bp
  • Oil WTI (10:50 PM): $84.93 -0.9%

Futures and Asia: Yahoo Finance and Bloomberg via swissinfo; ETFs and NVDA: Webull overnight trades at 12:37 AM ET. No overnight VIX quote was available; the 2-year shows Monday's close. No watchlist name moved 3% overnight.

Overnight, and what it means

  • US futures: S&P +0.1%, Nasdaq 100 +0.7%, Dow −0.3% at 10:37 PM ET; Nasdaq was still +0.5% at 10:50 PM.
  • Asia (10:50 PM ET): Topix −1.5%, ASX −1.7%, Hang Seng −0.8%, Shanghai flat; Euro Stoxx 50 futures −0.7%. The trigger was an interim US rule requiring licenses to ship advanced Nvidia and other AI chips to data centers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
  • Oil (10:50 PM ET): WTI $84.93 (−0.9%), Brent under $92, even with tanker attacks reported in Hormuz. Vice President Vance signaled the US wants to avoid a long war in Iran.
  • Rates, dollar, gold: 10-year 5.13% (flat), 30-year 5.48%, dollar −0.1%, yen 159.33, gold $3,872.58 (+0.4%), bitcoin $64,937 (−0.5%). Fed officials keep signaling a December hike; the minutes come out Wednesday.

Asia sold the chip curbs; US tech futures bought them back. That split says the curbs are a known worry and US traders lean toward Nvidia defending the group tonight. It challenges last night's "AI is being de-risked" force a little, but on thin overnight volume. Falling oil confirms the other force: it helps the DAL call and keeps XOM under your 2.0.

USO is under its 14, 30 and 50-day and has lost the 38.2% of the July–October run ($145.31); the 50% at $137.12 is next. Oil's short-term trend has turned down, which is a tailwind for airlines.

SPY at the open

The bounce off the Nov 5 low stalled under the 30/50-day band near $763, and Monday closed back under the triple-top neckline (about $749) for the second time. Overnight is flat at $739.50, so the open starts where the sellers left it: under the 14, 30 and 50-day, above the 200-day ($729.58).

Key levels: $757.17 · $749 neckline · $745 reclaim line · $739.50 overnight · $732.71 Nov 5 low · $729.58 200-day · $722.22 · $716.50 pattern target.

  • If SPY opens above $745… that's a retest of the broken floor. Don't chase calls into it. The act-now puts keep their own stops (PLTR $166.09, BA $171). A close over $745 ends the lean-short read.
  • If it holds between $732.71 and $745… the lean stays short. Take the act-now puts once the first 30 minutes settle, sized for Nvidia tonight.
  • If it opens below $732.71… the 200-day at $729.58 is the line. A close under it opens $722.22, then the triple-top target near $716.50. Don't add puts right into the 200-day; let it decide.

Movers on the list

  • INTC $54.76 (−1.3%): Traded as low as $52.65 after the close (−5.1%). I found no new company filing; the chip-license rule is the likely reason. The put moved past its best entry (plays below).
  • AMD $510.51 (+1.2%): US chip buyers stepped in overnight despite the Asia sale. Still under your 2.0 ($558.82).
  • BE $180.49 (+1.8%): Same bounce. Still above your 0.786 ($156.28).
  • XOM $165.64 (−0.7%): Under your 2.0 ($166.89) and the call's $166.50 stop line as oil slides.
  • HD (not ours) $344.37 (−0.9% after hours): Reports before the open; a read on the housing-linked consumer.

No watchlist name is moving 2% in the overnight session. On your ideas: SMH is $466.34, still $39 above your $427 line; DELL is $323.51 (+0.9%), above $295. Neither idea is closer this morning.

Your 0.5 ($155.33) is the floor under tonight; your 0.786 ($170.22) sits right at the top of the implied move. The options are pricing a trip to one of your levels, not past them.

  • Before the open: Home Depot (call 9:00 AM; estimate about $3.74 a share on about $41.1B revenue) and Disney (fiscal Q4; about $1.48 a share on about $25.1B). Release times weren't posted where I looked; both usually report around 6–7 AM.
  • After the close: Nvidia, about 4:20 PM, call 5:00 PM. It's on the watchlist. Its weekly options carry about 118% implied volatility; anyone holding NVDA options through the print gives most of that back tomorrow morning (IV crush).
  • Fed: no speakers found on today's calendar. FOMC minutes Wednesday. The Anthropic IPO is expected to price Wednesday and start trading as soon as Thursday.
  • A hot retail sales number would push yields up and turn this back into a rates story; a soft one keeps it a growth worry. Either way, it's the 8:30 move, not the day's move.

Plays check

  • PLTR Dec 18 $180 C · open: OFF. PLTR $159.75 overnight, under your 1.382 ($167.37) and $1.75 above the $158 close exit. Marked $372.50 (bid/ask $3.65/$3.80, OI 8,793), −$385. IV 52.9% vs moves 50.9% → FAIR. The idea is broken: three of your levels failed in order. I'd sell it today once the open settles rather than carry it through Nvidia. Nvidia exposure: High, both ways. A miss could gap it through $158 tomorrow with no chance to exit.
  • KO Dec 18 $100 C · open: STILL VALID. KO $99.37 overnight ($99.86 after hours). Stop a close below $97.38; target 1 $102.64. Marked $212.50 (bid/ask $2.05/$2.20, OI 4,312). IV 21.3% vs moves 17.2% → FAIR. The double-bottom target ($99.23) is already done, so take part at target 1. Nvidia exposure: Inverse. A bad Nvidia night pushes money into staples; a strong one can pull it out.
  • DAL Dec 18 $90 C · open: STILL VALID. DAL $86.53 overnight, $3.53 above the $83 stop (your 2.0 is $83.03). Marked $275 (bid/ask $2.60/$2.90, 10.9% spread), −$357.50. IV 40.0% → FAIR. Falling oil is the tailwind. Nvidia exposure: Low. Market beta only.
  • HLT Dec 18 $380 C · open: STILL VALID. HLT $373.83 (no overnight trades), 4.0% above the $359.41 exit. Marked $955 (bid/ask $8.40/$10.70; thin: OI 264, 3 traded), +$195. IV 25.0% → FAIR. Nvidia exposure: Low.
  • PLTR Dec 18 $150 P · level failure: ACT NOW. PLTR $159.75, under the $166.09 stop. From here it's 3.0 to 1: $19.04 to your 1.0 ($140.71) against $6.34 to the stop. Last $605 (bid/ask $5.95/$6.15, OI 10,191, 635 traded). IV 58.0% vs moves 50.9% → FAIR. The 200-day ($153.79) is the obstacle on the way. Better price: a bounce into $166–167.37 that closes back under. Risk at the stop: about $200–250. Nvidia exposure: High. A strong Nvidia print is the main way this gets stopped. If you take it, you're carrying it through tonight.
  • BA Dec 18 $165 P · level failure: ACT NOW. BA $164.94 overnight, a new low, under the $171 stop. 2.2 to 1 to your 1.0 ($151.70). Last $612.50 (bid/ask $6.00/$6.25, OI 6,302, 1,175 traded). IV 33.5% vs moves 36.1% → FAIR. Both double-top targets are already done, so it leans on the downtrend alone; that's why the stop stays tight. Risk at the stop: about $280. Nvidia exposure: Low. This is BA's own downtrend.
  • INTC Dec 18 $55 P · breakdown: TOO LATE. INTC $54.76 overnight. From here it's 1.3 to 1 ($3.25 to the $51.51 Nov 5 low against $2.44 to the $57.20 stop). It works again from $54.95, a 19-cent bounce; the better price is a failed bounce into $57.20. Last $445 (bid/ask $4.40/$4.50, OI 12,279). IV 72.6% vs moves 98.4% → CHEAP. Nvidia exposure: High. A good Nvidia night lifts every chip.
  • XOM Dec 18 $170 C · Fib flip pullback: CLOSER TO OFF. XOM $165.64 overnight, under your 2.0 ($166.89) and the $166.50 stop line. A close under $166.50 today cancels it. $477.50 (bid/ask $4.60/$4.95). IV 29.5% → FAIR. Nvidia exposure: None. Oil drives it, and oil is falling.
  • V Dec 18 $440 C · shallow pullback: WAIT. V $424.71 overnight, 0.4% above the $423 stop and 1.3% under the $430.18 trigger. The spread ($6.15/$7.15, 15%) fails the liquidity rule; it waits for both. Nvidia exposure: Low.
  • BA Dec 18 $170 P · failed rally: WAIT. $870 mid, over the $800 cap. Only the failed-rally entry into $179–181.5 (about $245 there) works; the $165 put is the act-now version. Nvidia exposure: Low.

If every open play hit its stop today, that's about $953 lost from last night's marks (about $1,500 from entry). Opening both act-now puts and getting stopped on both adds about $480.

Skipped today: anything on NVDA itself (weekly IV about 118% against 44.5% realized moves, 2.65 → EXPENSIVE), and the INTC put at this price (1.3 to 1).

Rejected at your 2.0, then lost the 1.618 and the 1.382 in order. That's a downtrend on your map, and the act-now put is the trade it gives.

New lows under every average, with the 50-day under the 200. The pattern targets are spent; the trend is what's left.

Alerts for today

  • SPY — price crosses above $745 → the floor is reclaimed; stop adding puts
  • SPY — price crosses below $729.58 → the 200-day gives way; $722.22 and $716.50 open up
  • PLTR — price crosses above $166.09 → the put's stop zone; a close there ends it
  • BA — price crosses above $171 → the put's stop; a close there ends it
  • INTC — price crosses above $54.95 → the put passes 1.5 to 1 again

An alert means look now, not buy now.

Opening rule of the day

On Nvidia day, let the first 30 minutes settle before taking the act-now puts, and use limit orders near the mid. Whatever you still hold at 4 PM is a bet on the print, so decide on the PLTR call before then.
